clue.text: A German entering pool is skinny

indicators.note: entering says the first pair of pieces goes inside the word for pool

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A thin German swimmer slips into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something thin and scanty, lacking in flesh or substance.

clue.text: I met star — terrible bully

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of the three words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone meets a celebrity who turns out to be a dreadful bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to treat them cruelly, which is a synonym in verb form.

clue.text: Fearful player in a scrum

indicators.note: in places the player inside the letters made by a and scrum

parts.note: a ruck is a loose scrum in rugby, or a crowded throng
West is one of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: A rugby player is frightened in the middle of a scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'player' is not a rugby player but a bridge seat: North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone overwhelmed with fear or wonder is full of dread and awe.

clue.text: Bloody unusual

definitions.meaning: meat that is barely cooked and still red inside

explanation.definitionFit: Underdone steak is described this way, and the same word means scarce or uncommon.

clue.text: Apprehension of Old Bill in court

indicators.note: in puts the pieces from Old and Bill inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: taken as written
a fee is a charge or bill for a service

explanation.surface: A nervous moment for the police when they have to appear in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, a picture the parse breaks into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is an idiom for losing nerve, a feeling of nervous dread before acting.

clue.text: Prefer one state of light

parts.note: to opt is to choose or prefer
I is the Roman numeral one
CAL is an abbreviation of California, a US state

explanation.surface: Choosing one particular condition of illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to sight and to the behaviour of visible radiation, as in optical physics.

clue.text: Uproar popular with union member creates a mess

parts.note: din is loud noise or uproar
in means fashionable or popular
a groom is one partner in a marriage, a union

explanation.surface: A trade union member causes a noisy and popular disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but here it is marriage; 'a mess' is not chaos but the military eating hall.
explanation.definitionFit: In the armed forces a mess is the place where people eat their meals together.

clue.text: Blunder has rascal guillotined

indicators.note: guillotined means beheaded, so the first letter of the word for rascal is cut off

parts.note: a terror is a naughty, troublesome child or rascal

explanation.surface: A blunder results in a scoundrel losing his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or slip is a plain synonym for a clumsy blunder.

clue.text: Suspicion about player's dazed state

parts.note: a trace or suspicion is a very slight amount, as in a suspicion of garlic
N, North, is one of the four bridge players

explanation.surface: A hint surrounding an actor's stupefied condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotic or half-conscious condition is a dazed state of mind.

clue.text: Horse in river causes worry

indicators.note: in places the horse inside the name of the river

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
gee-gee, GG, is a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A horse standing in a river is a cause for concern.

clue.text: Plant making weapon takes a lot of money

parts.note: a spear is a weapon
a mint is a large sum of money, as in to make a mint

explanation.surface: A factory producing arms rakes in a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory in the surface, but it is a herb.

clue.text: Roman dancing girl

indicators.note: dancing signals the letters of the word before it are moved about

explanation.surface: An Italian girl is out on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so an example of a girl, as crosswords allow.

clue.text: Judge to hold forth after scratching head

indicators.note: scratching the head means removing the first letter of the word for hold forth

parts.note: to orate is to speak at length, pompously

explanation.surface: A judge, puzzled, scratches their head before giving a lengthy speech.

clue.text: Selfish lad about to withdraw money

indicators.note: about says the boy's name goes round the next two pieces

parts.note: Eric is a boy's name, so a lad
to go is to leave or withdraw
a cent is a coin, a unit of money

explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning soon, but 'about' is the container and 'to withdraw' gives GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thinking only of themselves is self-centred and self-absorbed.

clue.text: Cloth worn by unfortunate in Kent

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton fabric
ill means unlucky, as in ill fortune

explanation.surface: Checked fabric is worn by some unlucky person in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; the answer is a town there.

clue.text: A coach I have becomes scathing

parts.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: Someone says their bus journey has made them bad-tempered.

clue.text: Poet playin' a prank

definitions.meaning: larking with its g dropped, meaning fooling about

explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin wrote The Whitsun Weddings; the dropped-g form of larking matches the dropped-g playin'.

clue.text: Isn't train moving? It's on it's way!

indicators.note: moving signals the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

clue.text: Manage brief response in leaflet

clue.text: Society destroys facilities

parts.note: kills means destroys

clue.text: Natural flavouring put in plonk or fruit drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'plonk' looks like the British word for cheap wine, but here it is the verb, to set down.

clue.text: Tell of soldier getting fresh

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, gives a soldier
late can mean recent or newest, as in the late news

parts.note: stale means old and no longer fresh

clue.text: Reservists went to announce a dance

clue.text: Proportion of a square in South American city

a T-square, so T

clue.text: It's cold in the tub for this lot
